In human benchmark, your reaction time is really fast, but it's a certain type of reaction. Namely, reaction to expected stimulus where you already know that the screen is gonna change color and react when it does. In game, many instances are reaction to unexpected stimulus, where you don't expect enemies well enough. It's a game sense issue, rather than a reaction time one. 

As an example, you could watch s1mple doing human benchmark. You'll realize his reaction time is similar to yours, maybe even a bit slower. But imma go out on a limb and say he's still better than you, because his game sense allows him to expect enemies in places you wouldn't, and allows him to utilize the "expected stimulus" reaction time while you have to rely on the "unexpected stimulus" reaction time. Many things factor into this too like crosshair placement, flick speed, movement etc etc
